Subject: MSA redlines — request to separate Hosted vs Dedicated economics

Hi Ben / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Brightline is excited about Redwood for inference. Our procurement team attached an MSA with a few targeted redlines. The main asks are:

- Partition the MSA so Hosted API usage (pay-as-you-go) and Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) are explicit exhibits with separate pricing and termination/true-up rules.
- Add a 30-day true-up window for Dedicated capacity (clarify overage billing cadence).
- Clarify data residency language for EU workloads (we can provide specific SOC2 evidence later).

I've attached Brightline_MSA_redline_v3.docx with inline comments. Can your legal team review and propose a redline that keeps our outstanding commercial terms intact while giving Brightline the contractual clarity for procurement?

We'd like to get to an internal procurement decision by the end of next week. Happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Jenna Sullivan
Head of Procurement
Brightline Systems

Subject: RE: MSA redlines — request to separate Hosted vs Dedicated economics

Team — I pulled Brightline's doc and sketched a proposed partition approach. High-level thoughts:

1) Partitioning: Agree with separate exhibits. I'll draft Exhibit B language that keeps Dedicated commitments and a clear monthly billing cadence for usage vs committed tokens. Brightline's 30-day true-up phrasing is reasonable — we should offer a 30-day reconciliation with a monthly invoice for any shortfalls/overages to match our finance ops.

2) Termination & credits: Brightline wants more graceful off-ramps for Dedicated within the first 6 months. We can offer a phased credit schedule (pro-rated over the first 6 months) but need to protect minimum commitment percentages after 90 days.

3) EU residency: We'll reference our Private deployment addendum and include a SOC2 summary link rather than heavy tech detail in the MSA. Procurement can accept evidence via the secure portal post-signature.

4) Action items:
- I'll produce a redline PDF (redwood_proposed_partition_terms.docx) with inline edits.
- Karthik, please confirm if commercial is comfortable with: (a) a 30-day reconciliation/ monthly overage invoice, and (b) the phased credit schedule for early termination.
- Ben, please offer Brightline two available call times tomorrow (8/27) for an hour max.

I'll aim for a draft by EOD 8/27 so we can iterate with procurement before their internal approval deadline.

— Neha Kapoor
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

Neha — that approach sounds good. Two commercial confirmations:

1) We can accept 30-day reconciliation with monthly invoicing for overages; that preserves our cashflow while meeting Brightline's cadence.
2) For the phased credit schedule: propose 75% credit in month 1, 50% month 2, 25% month 3 for any committed capacity cancelled inside the first 90 days — after 90 days, standard shortfall billing applies.

Rohan, Laura — flag if this deviates from expected go-to-market concessions.

Ben — please book the call window 8/27 3pm PT or 8/27 10am PT depending on Jenna's preference.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
